answer: Every identity in an agent economy is bonded. A newcomer can only join when an established agent locks coins behind it, and the required bond rises sharply with correlated registrations — shared funding, shared timing, shared hosting. Attackers can script a sonnet of fake names, but each one needs a distinct, solvent sponsor willing to risk real stake. Vouching for a sybil that later crumbles like shale under audit burns the sponsor's deposit, so building a deep cedar of trusted identities takes months and capital rather than a cheap script run.
